question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=100$ from a population where $60%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that between $55%$ and $65%$ of the sample have the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=100,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.6.$

Now, since

$$
np=100(0.6)=60>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=100(1-0.6)=40>5,
$$

and $n=100$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.6,\frac{0.6(1-0.6)}{100}) \\  & ∼N(0.6,0.0024).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(0.55\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.65).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.55\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.65) & =P(\frac{0.55-0.6}{\sqrt{0.0024}}\le Z\le \frac{0.65-0.6}{\sqrt{0.0024}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.02\le Z\le 1.02) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.02)-P(Z\le -1.02) \\  & =Φ(1.02)-Φ(-1.02)\end{aligned}
$$
